facts.text: **Scope.** This report covers only "App Services Context": the server-side platform that hosted Realm/Device Sync. It covers that platform's naming lineage (Stitch → MongoDB Realm → Atlas App Services), its deprecation and end-of-life (EOL), and which parts survived. It does not cover Device Sync internals (Flexible Sync, client reset, permissions mechanics), Realm SDK internals, or sibling concepts. Those belong to other frontier items.

In scope: Atlas App Services as the server-side container that hosted Device Sync. That covers the App object and its parts, how the parts interact during a sync session, the server-side invariants and limits that Sync users met, the product's naming history, and its end-of-life (EOL) state. It also covers the `context` global that App Services Functions receive, because a reader can easily confuse it with this concept's name.

43. Each Atlas Function receives a global `context` object with these parts: `context.app`, `context.environment`, `context.functions`, `context.http`, `context.request`, `context.services`, `context.user`, and `context.values`. 44. `context.app.deployment` describes the App's deployment model and region, for example `{"model": "LOCAL", "providerRegion": "aws-us-east-1"}`. 45. The example `hostingUri` value in the docs is `myapp-abcde.mongodbstitch.com`. 46. `context.request.rawQueryString` removes any query string key/value pair whose key is `secret` before the function sees it.

The App Services schema is separate from MongoDB's built-in schema validation, and the two can conflict. MongoDB advised either disabling built-in validation in favor of App Services schemas or managing the two layers so they are compatible. A document in a synced collection that does not conform to the App Services schema cannot be synced and is recorded in the __realm_sync.unsynced_documents collection; this includes documents written directly with tools such as mongosh or Compass. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/app-services/schemas.md
